entities.summary:
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a United Nations specialised agency created by the 1944 Chicago Convention to coordinate international civil aviation standards and air navigation policy. Headquartered in Montreal, it sets Standards and Recommended Practices that make cross-border flight technically interoperable.

Postwar aviation growth, jet travel, and security crises after hijackings and terrorism expanded ICAO’s agenda from airways to safety audits and facilitation. Member states negotiate through assemblies that translate technical consensus into annexes.

ICAO is the quiet constitutional backbone of global civil aviation.
